plan: With three bidders and values uniformly distributed on [0,49], the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n times my value, i.e., (2/3)*40 ≈ 26.7. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win, maximizing expected profit given the uniform distribution assumption for opponents' values.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3) × value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $13, so optimal bid ≈ $8.67. I'll round to $8.7 to slightly optimize for tie-breaking while staying close to theoretical optimum, ensuring positive expected profit if I win.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $17, so I should bid approximately 17 × 2/3 ≈ $11.30 to balance winning probability against profit margin. Bidding at or near this level maximizes expected profit given rational competitors likely use similar shading strategies.
